geography: California, statewide -- every operator on Cal-ITP's nightly ingest list
time_coverage: current statewide snapshot; refreshed and republished monthly (CKAN accrualPeriodicity R/P1M, metadata_modified 2026-07-21). Times are SCHEDULED clock times on a service day, not observed times.
schema_and_format: CSV, 23 columns: base64_url, trip_id, arrival_time, departure_time, stop_id, stop_sequence, stop_headsign, pickup_type, drop_off_type, continuous_pickup, continuous_drop_off, shape_dist_traveled, timepoint, arrival_sec, departure_sec, start_pickup_drop_off_window, end_pickup_drop_off_window, mean_duration_factor, mean_duration_offset, safe_duration_factor, safe_duration_offset, pickup_booking_rule_id, drop_off_booking_rule_id. arrival_sec/departure_sec are Cal-ITP additions: seconds from service-day start, which is the ONLY correct arithmetic basis for block chaining because GTFS clock times legitimately exceed 24:00:00 for after-midnight service (a trip ending '25:10:00' is 90600 s, and treating it as 01:10 would produce a negative gap). This is the largest object in the packet at ~2.83 GB and MUST be streamed, never loaded whole.
update_frequency: monthly (CKAN accrualPeriodicity R/P1M). source_checksum is null -- trust-on-first-use; the retained digest is recorded in calitp-gtfs-stop-times.acquired.json.
canonical_contract: app.canonical.entities.DeadheadSegment (Program A, ADR-0047). The first departure and last arrival of each trip become the boundaries between which a DeadheadSegment's started_at/ended_at are computed; the first and last stop_id become from_stop_ref/to_stop_ref. No canonical entity is created for a stop time itself -- StopTimeObservation is TELEMETRY (what a vehicle was observed doing) and this is a SCHEDULE, so mapping these rows onto it would assert observation where none exists.

quality_tests.name: header_carries_trip_key_and_second_offsets
quality_tests.description: the first line contains base64_url, trip_id, stop_sequence and both arrival_sec and departure_sec -- without the second offsets, after-midnight trips cannot be ordered correctly

quality_tests.name: second_offsets_agree_with_clock_times
quality_tests.description: on a sample of rows, arrival_sec equals the HH:MM:SS arrival_time parsed as seconds-from-service-day-start, so the Cal-ITP-added column can be trusted rather than re-derived

acceptance_threshold: downloads over plain HTTPS with no credential, is CSV, > 1 GB, header contains base64_url, trip_id, stop_sequence, arrival_sec and departure_sec.
retention_and_deletion: retain WHILE the deadhead derivation is being iterated, then reconsider. This single object is ~97% of the packet's bytes and is only ever read to produce a per-trip first-departure/last-arrival summary that is four orders of magnitude smaller. Once that summary is stable and evidenced, the raw object is a candidate for eviction: it is reproducible from the same URL, and the acquired-record preserves its content address either way.
